title: Council elects a new chair
text: Mara Quill was elected chair of the Larkspur Harbor Council on a 5 to 2 vote. She promised to settle the seawall debate before autumn.

title: Pike unveils seawall plan
text: Councilor Amos Pike presented a $14 million seawall project to protect the waterfront from flooding. The concrete wall would run along the shore at Gull Point.

title: Storm Ada batters the north pier
text: Storm Ada tore away 40 meters of the north pier and left Front Street under a foot of water. Residents worried the next storm would be worse.

title: The Brass Kettle turns ten
text: The Brass Kettle, the cafe Ines Quill opened on Front Street, celebrated ten years in business. Ines credits the fishing crews who stop in for coffee at dawn.

title: Who pays for the wall?
text: Records show Northgate Capital pledged $3 million toward the seawall. Northgate has also applied to build forty condos at Gull Point.

title: Eelgrass survey begins
text: Dr. Felix Arden of the Cove Field Station began a summer survey of the eelgrass beds at Gull Point. The beds shelter juvenile cod during their first year.

title: Boatworks owner speaks out
text: Otto Brandt, owner of Brandt Boatworks, said the seawall would cut his yard off from the water. Brandt Boatworks has built and maintained the town ferry since 1988.

title: Grant secured for the old light
text: Keeper Juno Reyes secured a state heritage grant to restore the lens of the Larkspur Light. Work on the lighthouse starts after the summer regatta.

title: Early findings alarm biologists
text: Arden's preliminary findings say construction at Gull Point would smother about 60 percent of the eelgrass. He urged the council to consider a living shoreline instead.

title: Librarian unearths 1903 charter
text: Librarian Wen Liu found the original 1903 harbor charter in a basement box at the Larkspur Library. It grants the public perpetual access to the shore at Gull Point.

title: Old charter clouds condo plans
text: Lawyers say the 1903 charter could block the Northgate condos, since the development would close public access. Juno Reyes called the charter the oldest promise the town ever made.

title: Regatta results
text: Sadie Brandt won the 2026 Larkspur Regatta in a skiff built at her father's yard. Entry fees from the race will go to the lighthouse restoration.

title: Ferry posts winter schedule
text: The Saltmarsh Ferry, captained by Sadie Brandt, will stop running on November 15 and resume on April 1. Riders can book the last crossing of the season online.

title: Seawall vote postponed
text: Chair Mara Quill postponed the seawall vote until the field station delivers its final eelgrass report. Councilor Pike objected, calling the delay reckless.

title: Packed house at flood forum
text: Residents packed The Brass Kettle for a forum on rising tides. Several said their basements now fill with water at every king tide.

title: Harvest Market heads indoors
text: The Saturday Harvest Market will move into the old net loft for the winter and open at 7:30 a.m. Organizer Ines Quill, sister of council chair Mara Quill, said vendors voted for the change.

title: Living shoreline test approved
text: The field station and Brandt Boatworks will build a 50-meter living shoreline of oyster reef and marsh grass at the north pier. If it holds through winter, it could become an alternative to the seawall.
